what_i_see: A thin S-shaped ribbon about 12 arcsec long, running north-south, with a bright yellowish knot at its centre and bluer, clumpy ends. A small bluish disc galaxy with its own nucleus sits about 5 arcsec north-east, touching the ribbon's northern tip. Unrelated red galaxies nearby.
most_likely: An interacting galaxy pair at z about 0.25-0.35: a disc galaxy pulled into two long tidal arms (integral-sign shape, roughly 45 kpc end to end) by the smaller companion to the north-east.
against_it: The northern arm is thin and curves around the companion somewhat like a lensed arc, but the S-shape, central bulge and low-mass blue 'lens' argue against lensing. Redshifts are photometric only.
decisive_test: One long-slit or IFU spectrum along the ribbon and through the companion: matching redshifts and a continuous velocity gradient confirm a tidal pair; a much higher arc redshift would mean lensing.
catalogue_notes: SIMBAD: nothing within 60 arcsec; no cluster or lens type within 5 arcmin (also NED, VizieR keyword search). NED: WISEA J041401.59-531138.1 at 0.3 arcsec, no redshift. REGALADE galaxies at 0.7 arcsec (z~0.26) and 5.1 arcsec (z~0.34+/-0.10). No Gaia source within 30 arcsec. X-ray source at 35 arcsec unrelated.
